subject: Catalyst Health: certification roadmap & FedRAMP scoping questions
messages:
From: Jacob Green <jacob.green@catalysthealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Aug 2028 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Certification roadmap & FedRAMP scoping questions

Hi Ben / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Catalyst Health is excited about the latency profile and deterministic routing you described. Before we proceed to procurement we need to validate a few certification and evidence items to satisfy our security team. Can you help clarify the following?

1) ISO 27001: do you have a published scope document or target certification date for ISO? If not, what components of the Redwood service are in-scope today (control plane, serving runtime, private deployment package)?

2) FedRAMP: do you have a FedRAMP sponsor or partner, and any planned timelines for a FedRAMP Tailored / Moderate path? If not, what is your recommended approach for regulated healthcare customers that require FedRAMP-equivalent controls?

3) Evidence / sampling: our auditors will request sample artifacts (logs, config snapshots, KMS rotation records, SOC2 reports). What is typical sample size and lead time to produce snapshot material for a pre-audit dry run?

4) Questionnaires: we prefer a completed SIG / CAIQ if possible for rapid assessment. Can you attach a current SQ/CAIQ or indicate who on your team can take that on?

If it's helpful I can share our security questionnaire up-front. We hope to lock a mutual action plan by Sept 8 to keep the procurement window intact.

Appreciate any detail you can provide.

Best,
Jacob Green
Director, Procurement & Security
Catalyst Health
[jacob.green@catalysthealth.com]

[Attachment: Catalyst_Sec_RFI.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Green <jacob.green@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Aug 2028 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Certification roadmap & FedRAMP scoping questions

Jacob — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up top, then a proposed next step (MAP).

1) ISO 27001: we do not yet have a final certificate to share. We have an internal ISO program targeting a submitted Statement of Applicability and external audit window in Q1 2029. Current in-scope components for the certification program are: the Redwood control plane, hosted Redwood API, and the Dedicated capacity offering. The Private package (customer-managed on-prem) is scoped as a separately attested artifact (we document boundary decisions in the scope draft).

2) FedRAMP: we do not currently hold a FedRAMP authorization and do not have an official federal sponsor arranged. For regulated healthcare customers we recommend a compensating-controls approach (tight boundary documentation + continuous monitoring options) while we evaluate a Moderate path; we can also facilitate introductions to a couple of marketplace partners who accelerate FedRAMP engagements.

3) Evidence / sampling: typical turnaround to produce curated snapshots and log extracts for a single auditor dry run is 3–5 business days once owners are engaged. For larger bundles (sampling across 6–8 controls) expect 7–12 business days. We maintain a prioritized evidence intake queue; I'll note that KMS rotation records and snapshotting for Dedicated pools are handled by different owners and can add lead time.

4) Questionnaires: attaching the current SIG checklist we use for pre-sales assessments; CAIQ is available on request (I can have Kimberly attach the latest CAIQ).

Proposed next step (mutual action plan):
- Today: we share SIG + ISO scope draft (attached).
- By Fri, Aug 25: Catalyst security to confirm which controls need sampling vs. assert-only.
- Week of Aug 28: technical evidence dry-run with our infra team (Kim will coordinate owners).
- By Sept 8: MAP agreed and procurement kickoff.

I will loop Grace O'Connor (program lead for certifications) to confirm audit windows and resource commitments.

Attachments included: SIG_CAIC_template.docx, iso-scope-draft.pdf

Let me know if you want a short sync (30m) this week.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: SIG_CAIC_template.docx (docx)]
[Attachment: iso-scope-draft.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jacob Green <jacob.green@catalysthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Aug 2028 13:37:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Certification roadmap & FedRAMP scoping questions

Adding a few technical clarifications from the compliance team:

- ISO scope draft (attached) currently excludes on-prem customer-managed enclaves; we document expected customer responsibilities in the Private package binder.
- For SOC2 / ISO artifact requests we usually provide time-bound log exports (UTC timestamps), snapshot of serving runtime config (kernel/quantization profile), and KMS key rotation logs. For Dedicated customers we can also provide a weekly KV-cache audit report if requested.
- On FedRAMP equivalence: our recommended immediate step is a control-gap mapping against FedRAMP Moderate. We can deliver a sample mapping (2–3 key controls) within 48 hours to show approach and tradeoffs.

Irene Choi and the control owners will need a concrete list of sample IDs to extract logs for a dry-run — that is the gating item for the 3–5 day turnaround Ben referenced. If Catalyst can identify 10–12 representative transactions/sessions per control area we can use them as sampling anchors.

I attached the current ISO scope draft here (redline) and the SIG template Ben attached is the most up-to-date.

Kimberly Park
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: iso-scope-draft.pdf (redline)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jacob Green <jacob.green@catalysthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Aug 2028 16:48:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Certification roadmap & FedRAMP scoping questions

Jacob — thanks for raising these. Quick operational confirmation from my side:

- We can commit an initial dry-run window the week of Aug 28 for one control-area bundle (logging + KMS + config snapshot). Kimberly will coordinate control owners and Irene will be the evidence intake point.
- Target: produce a dry-run artifact packet within 5 business days of sample IDs being provided. If Catalyst needs expanded sampling we will confirm resource impact and an updated delivery date.
- We do not want to overpromise FedRAMP timelines; however, if Catalyst prefers a FedRAMP-like posture now we will prioritize a FedRAMP mapping and provide a partner intro; that mapping can be delivered as an addendum within two business days after the dry-run.

Action items I will own:
- Confirm resource allocation for Aug 28 dry-run (by EOD Wed, Aug 23).
- Provide a template list of 12 sample anchors for Catalyst to choose from.

Jacob — would you prefer a 30-minute technical sync Thu Aug 24 or Fri Aug 25? If yes I will send a calendar invite and include the infra owners.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Programs
Redwood Inference
